said.text: Spawn agent that will do 2. With this tool

questions.text: Is the system idea 2 from the list: an authorization service in the style of Google Zanzibar or OpenFGA, where a check answers yes exactly when the stored relationship tuples derive it under the schema?
questions.assumed: Yes: relationship tuples, a schema of object types and relations, check, write and delete of tuples; listing objects only if it stays small.

questions.text: Which relation rules does the schema have?
questions.assumed: Four, as in Zanzibar: direct tuples (doc:1#viewer@user:ann); usersets as subjects (group:eng#member: everyone who is a member); a relation implied by another on the same object (an editor is a viewer); and a relation inherited through a link (a document's viewers include its parent folder's viewers). No exclusion or intersection.

questions.text: Groups nest and folders nest, so a derivation can be long. How deep does a check go?
questions.assumed: A fixed resolution depth, as OpenFGA's 25: a check follows at most that many steps (a userset, an implied relation or a link each is one step); what is derivable only in more steps is answered no. The depth is part of the configuration.

questions.text: Which tuples does a check read when writes happen around it?
questions.assumed: Each write and delete gets the next version (Zanzibar's zookie). A check names a version and answers exactly from the tuples the writes up to that version leave; it never mixes versions. A cache may speed checks up, but it never answers from another version's tuples.

Schema changes over time (one schema, fixed); exclusion, intersection and conditions; who may write tuples (authentication of callers); listing the users of an object; a watch API; replication across regions.
